topic: Variance estimation and hypothesis testing for repeated random train/test cross-validation estimates of generalization error and of differences between algorithms
own_question: How can the variance of the repeated-split cross-validation estimator be estimated so that tests and confidence intervals account for training-set as well as test-example variability?
actual_method_and_evidence: Theoretical decomposition of the variance into covariance terms. The paper argues that no general unbiased variance estimator that is linear or quadratic in the losses exists. It proposes two estimators: a corrected resampled t-test, which uses the heuristic correlation n2/n with the variance factor (1/J+n2/n1), and a conservative Z based on half-splits. Simulations use 1000 datasets each for regression, Gaussian classification, and subsampled UCI letter recognition. Naive t and resampled t tests were often liberal. The corrected tests showed size closer to nominal, but they were sometimes liberal or conservative. Data are assumed i.i.d.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Overlapping repeated train/test splits produce correlated fold estimates. Treating them as independent can underestimate variance and make comparisons appear significant too often.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: Sec. 2, Eq. (8); Sec. 4 items 2 and 5; Table 1
claim_checks.qualification: Shown for i.i.d. examples under random subsampling. Our time-series campaign is not i.i.d., so this supports caution only, not a validated correction.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Paired loss differences between two estimators on shared splits are a standard object for statistical comparison.
claim_checks.qualification: Their reported performance comes from the authors' simulations, not from fusion data.

validation_if_relevant: Random subsampling with J around 15 and M of 5 to 10 is recommended for i.i.d. data. The paper offers no temporal, blocked, or shot-wise design.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim that corrected resampled t or conservative Z is valid for autocorrelated shot/time data.
Do not claim that we used these tests unless they were actually implemented.
Do not generalize to all CV practice in fusion.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Useful as statistical background for uncertainty when comparing estimators across validation designs. Its i.i.d. assumption limits direct transfer to our data.
